page: Vultr vcg-a40-2c-10g-4vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with an Intel x86_64 processor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes a 16 MB L3 cache and supports AVX, AES, and FMA instructions. The system is equipped with 10.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.0 GB per core.

This instance includes a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU allocation of approximately 0.0833, providing 4 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage consists of a bundled 180 GB NVMe SSD. Additionally, the instance is provisioned with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates average single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1462.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1777.17. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics fall into the weak category, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2603.0 and memory write speeds of 20.61 GB/sec. Despite these limitations, the fractional GPU configuration demonstrates strong performance in LLM inference prompt processing, achieving 3480.67 tokens/sec for a small 135M model and 202.17 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model.

By utilizing a fractional GPU slice, this server offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads requiring GPU acceleration without the expense of a full dedicated card. It is best suited for lightweight machine learning inference, small-scale LLM prompt processing, and development or testing environments that require CUDA or Ampere architecture capabilities alongside moderate NVMe storage. It is less suitable for heavy multi-threaded CPU tasks, database operations, or high-throughput web serving.
